Kirkwood council to use existing permit process on Billy G's, Four Hands noise
Council members said the special use permit process, not the stalled noise ordinance rewrite, will address complaints about outdoor music at the two businesses.
The Kirkwood City Council, during a work session held Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026, decided to address noise complaints about Billy G's and Four Hands through the existing special use permit process rather than waiting on a broader noise ordinance rewrite.
A council member said updating the full noise ordinance could take months, while residents near the businesses continue to be affected. "We can sit here and talk about this for six months and talk about all these things that Deb has bring up which is are good points but in the meantime these poor people that live by Billy G's are getting blasted out," the member said.
THE IMMEDIATE FIX Asked what would happen with Billy G's and Four Hands while the ordinance work continues, a council member said, "We follow the SUP," and another responded, "We move that one forward tonight." One member confirmed the special use permit process could handle the situation "without this ordinance" and "without any police intervention."
ENFORCEMENT CONCERNS A council member identified as Deb raised broader concerns about enforceability of any new noise rules, saying the city lacks an acoustical engineer or sound expert. "I don't think this ordinance is in a place yet for us to spend a lot of time on to really make these kinds of decisions," she said, adding she is "not in favor of rush rushing this through just to come up with a decibel reading."
NEXT STEPS Council members discussed forming a subcommittee or holding a dedicated work session with an outside expert to continue the broader noise ordinance discussion, separate from the Billy G's and Four Hands matter. City staff member Darren said he would email a list of recommended changes to start that process.
